mcat_description.short: A prefabricated steel-framed roofing shed structure purpose-built to cover one or more badminton courts, sold as a supply-only or supply-and-erect package in the Indian market. Typically constructed using MS/PEB portal frames with colour-coated metal, PPGI, or polycarbonate roofing sheets.
mcat_description.long: Badminton Court Roofing Sheds are purpose-engineered overhead enclosure structures designed to cover standard BWF-dimension badminton courts (13.4 m × 6.1 m per court), requiring a minimum clear height of 9 m under the truss as per BWF indoor court standards. The primary structural system is either a Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) portal frame or an MS tubular/truss frame, with roofing in colour-coated PPGI, GI, polycarbonate, or FRP sheets, and optional insulation via sandwich panels or air-bubble foil. These sheds are sold across India by fabricators and PEB manufacturers as turnkey construction services or as prefabricated supply-and-erect packages, customised for single-court, double-court, or multi-court configurations. Key buyer requirements include wind and rain resistance, adequate natural or artificial lighting, ventilation, and structural compliance with IS 800 (steel structures) and relevant seismic zone requirements.

market_context: Badminton Court Roofing Sheds are a well-established product category in the Indian prefabricated structures market, driven by rapid growth in badminton as a sport across schools, academies, residential societies, and corporate campuses. The dominant structural system in the Indian market is either a PEB (Pre-Engineered Building) portal frame or an MS tubular/truss frame, with PPGI (pre-painted galvanised iron) colour-coated sheets being the most common roofing material; polycarbonate and FRP sheets are used where natural light transmission is prioritised. BWF standards require a minimum clear height of 9 m from floor to ceiling for indoor courts, which directly drives the structural height specification buyers request. Standard court footprint is 13.4 m × 6.1 m per court (doubles), and sheds are commonly configured for single, double, or multi-court layouts with additional buffer space. Sellers are concentrated in South India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh/Telangana), Maharashtra, and Gujarat, with Tamil Nadu (Chennai) being a particularly active fabrication hub. The product is sold both as a supply-only prefabricated structure and as a turnkey supply-and-erect service; buyers typically request engineering drawings and structural calculations as part of the package. IS 800 (Code of Practice for General Construction in Steel) is the relevant Indian standard for the structural steel framework. The keyword signal 'badminton court roofing shed jsw' confirms JSW Steel as a recognised brand reference for roofing sheet material in buyer vocabulary.
